req.title: Session cookie has HttpOnly attribute
req.statement: The system shall set HttpOnly on the session cookie.

doc.reasoning: The requirement mandates that the session cookie carries the HttpOnly attribute. To test this we must trigger session-cookie issuance (login), then inspect the Set-Cookie response header. Three angles are needed: (1) positive – successful login sets a cookie with HttpOnly; (2) negative – a request that never creates a session (e.g. GET /auth/login) must NOT produce a session cookie with HttpOnly (or any session cookie at all), confirming the attribute is tied to session creation; (3) boundary – the HttpOnly flag must appear as an exact token in the header string, not merely as a substring of another attribute name, and the response status must be exactly 302 (redirect after login), not any other 2xx. All tests use in-process app.test_client() with a temp SQLite database pre-seeded by init_db(), and assert exact values to maximise mutation kill rate.

tests.name: test_session_cookie_has_httponly_on_login
preconditions: Flask app created with TESTING=True and a fresh temp database
Database initialised with init_db() so user 'Rahul'/'stone' exists
actions: Inspect the Set-Cookie header of the response
expected: The HttpOnly attribute token appears in the Set-Cookie header (case-insensitive)
trace: R-FLASKR-043: session cookie has HttpOnly attribute
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

def test_session_cookie_has_httponly_on_login():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    set_cookie = r.headers.get('Set-Cookie', '')
    assert set_cookie != '', 'Set-Cookie header must be present after login'
    assert 'session' in set_cookie.lower()
    # HttpOnly must appear as an exact attribute token
    tokens = [t.strip().lower() for t in set_cookie.split(';')]
    assert 'httponly' in tokens, f'HttpOnly not found in Set-Cookie tokens: {tokens}'

test_session_cookie_has_httponly_on_login()

tests.name: test_no_session_cookie_on_unauthenticated_get
preconditions: Flask app created with TESTING=True and a fresh temp database
Client sends GET /auth/login (no credentials, no session created)
actions: Inspect the Set-Cookie header of the response
expected: Either no Set-Cookie header is present, or any Set-Cookie header does NOT contain a 'session' cookie with HttpOnly (no session is established)
trace: R-FLASKR-043: HttpOnly is only relevant when a session cookie is actually issued; a plain GET must not issue one
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

def test_no_session_cookie_on_unauthenticated_get():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.get('/auth/login')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    set_cookie = r.headers.get('Set-Cookie', '')
    # If a Set-Cookie is present it must NOT be a session cookie with HttpOnly
    # (no login occurred, so no authenticated session should be set)
    if set_cookie:
        tokens = [t.strip().lower() for t in set_cookie.split(';')]
        # A session cookie with HttpOnly should NOT appear here
        has_session_name = set_cookie.lower().startswith('session=')
        if has_session_name:
            # If somehow a session cookie is set, it still must not be HttpOnly
            # (this branch documents the negative expectation)
            assert 'httponly' not in tokens, (
                'Unexpected HttpOnly session cookie on unauthenticated GET'
            )

test_no_session_cookie_on_unauthenticated_get()

tests.name: test_httponly_token_is_exact_not_substring
preconditions: Flask app created with TESTING=True and a fresh temp database
Database initialised with init_db() so user 'Anjali'/'cloud' exists
actions: Check that 'httponly' appears as a standalone trimmed token, not embedded in another attribute name
expected: Set-Cookie header contains 'HttpOnly' as a standalone semicolon-delimited token
The token list does NOT contain any token that merely contains 'httponly' as a substring of a longer word
trace: R-FLASKR-043: HttpOnly must be a proper cookie attribute, not an accidental substring match
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

def test_httponly_token_is_exact_not_substring():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Anjali', 'password': 'cloud'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    set_cookie = r.headers.get('Set-Cookie', '')
    assert set_cookie != '', 'Set-Cookie header must be present'
    tokens = [t.strip() for t in set_cookie.split(';')]
    lower_tokens = [t.lower() for t in tokens]
    # Exact match: one token must be exactly 'httponly'
    assert 'httponly' in lower_tokens, (
        f'HttpOnly not present as exact token; tokens={lower_tokens}'
    )
    # Boundary: no token should be a longer word that merely contains 'httponly'
    for tok in lower_tokens:
        if 'httponly' in tok:
            assert tok == 'httponly', (
                f'Token "{tok}" contains httponly but is not exactly httponly'
            )

test_httponly_token_is_exact_not_substring()

tests.name: test_session_cookie_httponly_after_failed_login_not_set
preconditions: Flask app created with TESTING=True and a fresh temp database
Client POSTs invalid credentials (wrong password) to /auth/login
actions: Inspect response status and Set-Cookie header
expected: Response status is exactly 200 (login page re-rendered, not redirected)
No authenticated session cookie with HttpOnly is issued (login failed)
trace: R-FLASKR-043: HttpOnly session cookie must only be issued on successful authentication, not on failed login
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

def test_session_cookie_httponly_after_failed_login_not_set():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'wrongpassword'})
    # Failed login must re-render the form, not redirect
    assert r.status_code == 200
    set_cookie = r.headers.get('Set-Cookie', '')
    # If any Set-Cookie is present, it must not be an authenticated session
    # i.e. no HttpOnly session cookie should carry a real user_id
    if set_cookie:
        tokens = [t.strip().lower() for t in set_cookie.split(';')]
        # A session cookie here would be empty/cleared, not an authenticated one
        # We assert HttpOnly is NOT present on a failed-login response
        assert 'httponly' not in tokens, (
            f'HttpOnly session cookie must not be set on failed login; tokens={tokens}'
        )

test_session_cookie_httponly_after_failed_login_not_set()

tests.name: test_session_cookie_httponly_present_for_multiple_users
preconditions: Flask app created with TESTING=True and a fresh temp database
Database initialised with init_db() so users James/river and Diya/cloud exist
Two separate test clients simulate two independent login sessions
actions: POST /auth/login with username=James, password=river using client1
POST /auth/login with username=Diya, password=cloud using client2
Inspect Set-Cookie headers from both responses
expected: Both Set-Cookie headers contain 'HttpOnly' as an exact token
trace: R-FLASKR-043: HttpOnly must be set consistently for every user session, not just the first
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

def test_session_cookie_httponly_present_for_multiple_users():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
    for username, password in [('James', 'river'), ('Diya', 'cloud')]:
        client = app.test_client()
        r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': username, 'password': password})
        assert r.status_code == 302, f'Expected 302 for {username}, got {r.status_code}'
        set_cookie = r.headers.get('Set-Cookie', '')
        assert set_cookie != '', f'No Set-Cookie for {username}'
        assert set_cookie.lower().startswith('session='), (
            f'Cookie name is not session for {username}: {set_cookie}'
        )
        tokens = [t.strip().lower() for t in set_cookie.split(';')]
        assert 'httponly' in tokens, (
            f'HttpOnly missing for {username}; tokens={tokens}'
        )

test_session_cookie_httponly_present_for_multiple_users()
